newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian interest rates may rise by yr-end-I-Sec.
newsitem.headline: Indian interest rates may rise by yr-end-I-Sec.

text.p: Rising money supply trends in the Indian economy could push up interest rates towards the end of financial year 1997/98 (April-March), ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said on Wednesday.
"The surge in broad money supply (M3) continues with the growth rate for the first quarter having touched 16.78 percent," the securities firm said in its latest Debt Market Update.
The Reserve Bank of India said year-on-year money supply growth rose to 16.8 percent on June 20 from 16.6 percent on June 6. The money supply growth a year ago was 15.5 percent.
The Reserve Bank aims to hold money supply growth at 15.0-15.5 percent in 1997/98 (April-March).
The option of funding the oil pool deficit through the fiscal deficit, if implemented, would have a further expansionary impact on money supply, the I-Sec report said.
The oil pool deficit, or money owed by the federal government to oil firms for selling their products at prices well below international levels, presently stands at over 150 billion rupees.
"Apart from fuelling inflation, this would also imply an increase in absolute level of the fiscal deficit and hence higher market borrowings for the year to that extent."
"Though any immediate impact on interest rates can be ruled out, such a measure could put an upward pressure on rates towards the end of the financial year," the report said.
